subject.title: fix(daemon): route systemd restarts through SIGUSR1

question: Should generated systemd service-manager restarts be allowed to use the SIGUSR1 restart path when `commands.restart=false` blocks external SIGUSR1?
rationale: The patch cannot distinguish a systemd `RestartKillSignal=SIGUSR1` from a manual external SIGUSR1 in Node, so preserving the documented disabled-restart contract versus enabling systemd managed restart recovery requires maintainer intent.

options.title: Preserve disabled-restart compatibility
options.body: Keep `commands.restart=false` from turning `systemctl restart` into an ignored SIGUSR1, even if that means using a different systemd handoff shape or deferring this directive until the policy can distinguish service-manager restarts.

options.title: Let generated systemd bypass the block
options.body: Treat installed systemd units as trusted restart controllers and update code, docs, and tests to state that `commands.restart=false` does not block service-manager restarts for generated units.

options.title: Pause this systemd shortcut
options.body: Leave generated units on SIGTERM restarts until a broader restart-policy design handles service-manager and manual OS-signal restarts separately.

recommendation.title: Preserve disabled-restart compatibility
recommendation.body: Keep `commands.restart=false` from turning `systemctl restart` into an ignored SIGUSR1, even if that means using a different systemd handoff shape or deferring this directive until the policy can distinguish service-manager restarts.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent merged history owns both the generated systemd unit template and the SIGUSR1 external-restart policy lines implicated by this compatibility choice.
